findings.title: `hasattr` guard in `tick.py` is a documented boundary compromise
findings.description: The `if hasattr(spatial, "record_density"): spatial.record_density(filtered_counts)` line in `tick.py` introduces a duck-typed backdoor to the spatial layer that is not part of the `SpatialQuery` protocol. The slice doc explicitly considers the alternative (add `record_density` to the protocol with a default no-op) and rejects it as "couples the protocol to a dispatcher concern that no other backend needs." The trade-off is well-reasoned and documented, and the per-tick cost is trivial — but `tick.py` now carries implicit knowledge that some spatial implementations may expose a density-record hook. This is the right call given the constraints, and the rationale is sound; raising as a NOTE for visibility, not as an action item.
